title: GynCycle menstrual period shows no rate-limiting parameter under ±10% OAT sensitivity; sensitivity is loop-distributed, surge-weighted
paragraph:
Fine sweeps (0.5×–1.5×) of the four task-named candidate levers:
`k_Ih_FSH` (V_FSH) flat (28.0–28.2 d, S = +0.002, rank 92 — the "higher FSH → shorter
cycle" law is **not** reproduced and the weak sign is reversed); `T_E2_LH` (Km,LH surge
threshold) 26.9–28.5 d (S = +0.047, rank 46, longer-when-higher); `k_AF2_AF3`
(follicular mass-transfer) 27.4–29.1 d (S = −0.063, rank 35, shorter-when-higher);
`k_cl_Lut4` (corpus-luteum decay) **26.1–35.1 d** (S = −0.222, rank 23,
shorter-when-higher) — the widest-range lever among the fine-swept candidates (the 4
named nodes + top-5 local movers; not a claim over all 114 params), i.e. the luteal
timer is tunable in the model. All perturbations across all four sweeps stayed stable
(21/21 each).

title: Mahdessian 2021 \u2014 single-cell temporal transcriptomics of the human cell\
paragraph:
The modern gold-standard human dataset for the **cell-cycle layer** as a continuous oscillator
(Mahdessian, Cesnik, Gnann et al., *Nature* 2021, "Spatiotemporal dissection of the cell cycle
with single-cell proteogenomics"). **1,152 single U2OS cells** profiled by Smart-seq2 scRNA-seq
(`geo:GSE146773`), each carrying a **measured FUCCI fluorescence position** that places the cell
at a continuous coordinate (pseudotime) around the cell cycle — not just discrete G1/S/G2M bins.
A companion single-cell proteomics layer lives in the Human Protein Atlas, with analysis code
openly released.

title: NHANES reproductive-state biomarker-confounding \u2014 breadth scale-up
paragraph:
**Mechanism confirmed by composition (Model C).** The cluster is driven by the
**estrogen-containing** component, not progestin-only — e.g. hsCRP: estrogen-combined
**+230%** (p=2e-27) vs progestin-only +25% (n.s.); the same estrogen-specific pattern
holds for triglycerides, ferritin, and albumin. This is the textbook oral-estrogen
hepatic first-pass signature.

title: Activity-glucose coupling strength trends protective across glycemic outcomes
paragraph:
In CGMacros (n=34 subjects with an actigraphy↔CGM daily-profile coupling row joined 1:1 to the
clinical panel `bio.csv`), age+BMI-adjusted partial Spearman (fully rank-based; Pearson as
sensitivity) of coupling coherence against metabolic outcomes: every glycemic/insulin-resistance
outcome trends protective — fasting glucose ρ=−0.29 (p=0.11), HOMA-IR ρ=−0.26 (p=0.16), A1c
diabetes class ρ=−0.24 (p=0.19), HbA1c ρ=−0.21 (p=0.25), insulin ρ=−0.21 (p=0.26) — i.e. higher
coupling → healthier glycemia. HDL is nominally positive (ρ=+0.40, raw p=0.022) but fails BH-FDR
across the 10-outcome family (q=0.22) and weakens under Pearson (r=0.28); the lipid block is
mixed (total cholesterol/LDL also positive). Coverage is not a confounder: coherence vs
`coupling_coverage` ρ=+0.22 (p=0.22) and vs `n_cycles_or_days` ρ=−0.26 (p=0.14), both
non-significant, and the coverage-adjusted sensitivity column barely moves the estimates. The
n=34 minimum detectable correlation is ≈0.47 (80% power, α=0.05), above every observed |ρ| (≤0.40),
so this is a single-cohort, between-person, **direction-consistent but non-arbitrating** signal:
the uniform protective sign across glycemic outcomes — not any single coef

title: Homeostatic-Dysregulation cross-check concords with the KDM clock acceleration
paragraph: Cross-check on the same SWAN clock-marker rows: Homeostatic Dysregulation (HD), the Mahalanobis distance of each standardized marker vector from the premenopausal reference, with a NumPy Ledoit-Wolf (2004) shrinkage estimate of the reference covariance (shrinkage delta 0.005; full-panel condition number 614 -> 311 shrunk, and 11 -> 11 when LDL is dropped to break the Friedewald near-collinearity). Natural-postmenopause vs premenopause raises HD by +0.15 in the race-adjusted model (M2b, p=6.3e-6) and +0.11 within-person (M3, p=6.1e-3), same sign as the KDM clock and within-person robust; spline-age stable (+0.15 -> +0.15). KDM and HD are two different composite constructions on the same markers/cohort, so their agreement establishes construction-robustness (the result is not an artifact of the specific KDM aggregation algebra) - not cohort independence.

title: Cross-rhythm coupling strength carries metabolic-state information beyond static
paragraph:
In CGMacros (n=34 subjects with an actigraphy↔CGM coupling row joined to the clinical panel),
age+BMI-adjusted partial Spearman shows coupling coherence trending **protective across every
glycemic/insulin-resistance outcome** (fasting glucose, HbA1c, HOMA-IR, insulin, A1c diabetes
class; all negative ρ, −0.21 to −0.29), with HDL nominally positive (adj ρ=+0.40, raw p=0.022).
Coverage is not a confounder (coherence vs `coupling_coverage` ρ=+0.22 p=0.22; vs nights ρ=−0.26
p=0.14), so the signal is not a coverage artifact (`observation:cgmacros-coupling-metabolic-direction`).

title: Melbourne NeuroVista \u2014 chronic iEEG seizure timing (multidien / circamonthly\
paragraph:
Per-subject seizure / inter-ictal-activity event times with absolute timestamps over months-to-~2
years; open figshare download (CC-BY-NC-4.0).

title: Rest-activity amplitude (M10) is nearly collinear with total activity volume
paragraph: In the NHANES PAM 2011-2012 (_G) adult frame (n=2,068), the rest-activity-rhythm amplitude exposure M10 (mean activity over the 10 most-active hours) correlates with the coverage-normalized total daily activity volume (mean_daily_mims) at r=0.96 (collinearity_diagnostics.csv). Interdaily stability (IS, the regularity exposure) is far less volume-collinear at r=0.40; the secondary exposures range |r|<=0.43. Because M10 and volume are near-collinear, the Model C (activity-volume-adjusted) M10 coefficient is a high-variance residual-M10 contrast (peak activity at fixed daily volume), not a clean estimate of rhythm structure independent of activity amount. The diagnostic signature is visible in the coefficients: every significant M10 effect GROWS in magnitude from Model B to Model C (HbA1c -0.0035 -> -0.0368 log-units/SD; LDL +4.9 -> +11.3 mg/dL/SD; total cholesterol +4.5 -> +9.6 mg/dL/SD), the classic suppression pattern under collinearity.

title: Hughes 2009 — high-temporal-resolution mouse-liver circadian transcriptome
paragraph:
Hughes et al. 2009 ("High-temporal-resolution profiling of mouse liver"), GEO
**GSE11923**: Affymetrix Mouse Genome 430 2.0 (GPL1261), **48 arrays sampled every
1 h over 48 h** in **constant darkness (CT)** — the densest mouse-liver circadian
transcriptome time-course. This is the Hogenesch-group dataset that Robles, Cox &
Mann 2014 compared their liver **proteome** against.

title: A stochastic follicular-cohort extension of the Selgrade DDE reproduces the Ecochard2024 2–4-cycle cycle-length memory at the antral timescale, while within-cycle noise produces none — supporting cycle-length memory as a follicular-cohort readout
paragraph:
This **supports** `proposition:0011` with a clean, falsification-structured simulation
test. Adding stochastic follicular recruitment to the arm-1 Selgrade/Harris-Clark DDE and
sweeping the follicular-cohort maturation-window width `W` shows: **within-cycle noise
(W = 1) produces no cycle-length memory** (ACF horizon 0 — flat — *despite the highest CV,
0.20*, so it is not a variance artifact), while a **multi-cycle cohort produces memory of
horizon W − 1** in a clean monotone dose–response. **Widths 3, 4, and 6 cycles meet the
2–4-lag statistical horizon; the ~3–4-cycle (≈ 85–112 d) subset is the biologically
antral-timescale match** (W = 6 ≈ 168 d also clears the band but is longer than the antral
window). Significance is an *Ecochard-style* cycle-order-swap test on the **ACF** (PACF
reported but not tested; 2000 draws, lighter than the paper's 5000 + Bonferroni). The
result the experiment could have failed: a multi-cycle cohort might have left no readable
memory (luteal reset each cycle) or required an implausible timescale; it did neither.

paragraph:

paragraph:
Confirmatory metrics (both global, on the paired set N = 2,778; rhythmicity called per layer at

paired, inside [3%,10%]):

title: Deota 2023 — multi-tissue diurnal transcriptome under time-restricted feeding (22 organs, GSE190389)
paragraph:
Around-the-clock bulk RNA-seq of ~22 mouse tissues and brain regions (Deota et al. 2023,
*Cell Metabolism* 35(1):150–165), sampling every 2 h over 24 h under **ad libitum vs
9 h time-restricted feeding (TRF)** of Western diet. The GEO super-series
**GSE190389** (*Mus musculus*, ~1,677 samples) maps how feeding time, independent of
photic cues, reorganises rhythmic transcription across peripheral organs and brain
regions, including duodenum, and shows TRF reshapes nutrient-handling and clock-output
programs disrupted by mistimed eating.

title: Does uncontrolled season-of-collection introduce a systematic confound in human
paragraph: Wucher et al. (2023) show that 91.1% of expressed human protein-coding genes are differentially expressed across seasons in at least one of 46 tissues (GTEx v8, 932 donors), and that this seasonal transcriptome variation is orthogonal to day-night variation (Spearman rho = −0.12, P = 0.41). The scale and orthogonality of the seasonal signal raise the question: do published human transcriptomic, proteomic, and epigenomic disease studies that did not record or control for season-of-collection carry a systematic seasonal confound that is independent of, and additive to, the already-documented circadian confound from time-of-day?

title: Seasonal rhythms in human physiology, omics, biomarkers, cognition, and immunity
paragraph: The seasonal endocrine reorganisation documented in Tendler2021 has direct implications for h02: clinical reference ranges for cortisol, T3/T4, testosterone, estradiol, and IGF-1 that are not stratified by season can produce systematic misclassification at the extremes. The amplitudes are modest (2–10% of the distribution range) but systematic and year-consistent, meaning they compound across large cross-sectional studies that aggregate tests without season adjustment.

title: Analysis plan — coupling strength/phase-lag as an h01 homeostatic-control readout (CGMacros / BIDSleep / MMASH)
paragraph:
Verified empirically this session: CGMacros coupling `coherence` med 0.229 (range
0.005–0.596, 34/34 non-null); BIDSleep `coherence` med 0.187 (range 0.008–0.463,
82/82 non-null). Both are real, varying signals. CGMacros `bio.csv` is N=45 × 24
columns and carries the full metabolic panel; the 34 coupling subjects are a subset.

title: Weighted CYCLOPS (still sub-gate) plus a gate-clearing clean-room projection localize the
paragraph:
The second, **method-independent** test of `proposition:0007`. Under the same 20%-seed-drop
perturbation budget on TCGA-BRCA luminal-A (independent per-arm RNG masks), using the WP-D
signature's per-gene weights *inside* CYCLOPS lifts ordering stability from median Spearman 0.10 to
**0.61** — recovering most of the stability the flat consensus seed lost, but still **failing** the
pre-registered 0.90 gate. A **clean-room signature-only weighted cosinor projection** (Ueda 2004
molecular-timetable lineage; no autoencoder, no GPLv3 engine) on the *same* signature and *same* 498
tumors clears the gate at median Spearman **0.90** (concordance 0.88; a narrow margin). TC#3 scores
the projection magnitude (CMag-analogue) rank, not the inferred phase. The pre-registered 2×2
decision table maps this (weighted FAIL, projection PASS) onto cell `cyclops_autoencoder_fault`: the
circadian prior is usable as a stable strength ranking and the substrate carries recoverable
circadian-strength structure, so the instability is **localized to the CYCLOPS autoencoder on
single-timepoint LumA**. This `supports` proposition:0007's reading that the *CYCLOPS
ordering method* (not the seed) is the binding defi

title: Does circadian blood pressure dipping status moderate the effect of antihypertensive
paragraph: BedMed enrolled a general hypertensive primary-care population without pre-stratifying on circadian BP dipping status. Approximately 30–40% of hypertensive patients are non-dippers (nocturnal systolic BP fall <10% of daytime) or reverse-dippers (nocturnal systolic BP higher than daytime). These patients have higher cardiovascular risk and — on the mechanistic hypothesis that bedtime dosing is beneficial precisely because it shifts the antihypertensive peak to the nocturnal window — would be the subpopulation most likely to benefit. The question is whether BedMed's null finding reflects masking of a real benefit in non-dippers by null or adverse effects in dippers.

title: NHANES PAM actigraphy \u2192 rest-activity rhythm metrics (ingest probe)
paragraph:
Ran end-to-end (`code/workflows/nhanes-pam`); outputs in `results/nhanes-pam-actigraphy/`
(`rar_table.parquet`, `coverage_report.md`). **14,693 seen → 3,211 passed the coverage gate
(`included`) → 3,200 with a complete, in-range primary feature vector (`metric_complete`).**
The 11 gate-passing-but-incomplete rows (9 with a NaN primary metric, 2 with RA just outside
[0,1] from masking) are flagged `metric_complete=False` and excluded from distributions and
hard-bound checks. All **hard** sanity checks pass at **1.000** over `metric_complete`
(M10>L5, RA/IS/IV in range), plus **grid preserved 100%**, **clock-reconstruction match 100%**
vs PAXDAYM, and daytime M10-acrophase (97%, soft). M10-center acrophase (median 14.8 h) and
the secondary cosinor acrophase (14.9 h) agree — independent phase cross-check. Metric medians
(M10 15.9, L5 0.91, RA 0.89, IS 0.39, IV 0.43) sit in the published NHANES RAR range.

title: Bias Audit: METABRIC tertile CMag prognosis pre-registration (pre-reg:0003)
paragraph:
**Method note — this is a two-pass audit.** Pass 1 was the artifact author's self-pass (see Author
Independence below — by construction it under-rates author-side selection effects). Pass 2 was an
**independent adversarial reviewer** with no authorship stake, briefed to *falsify* 0003's legitimacy.
Where the two diverge, the independent verdict is recorded as authoritative. The independent reviewer
correctly predicted *in advance* which two biases the self-pass would under-rate (Threats §2, §5
below) — that prediction held, and those ratings are taken from the independent pass.

title: Analysis plan — METABRIC independent validation of the Ueda CMag index (t046 q77 part 1)
paragraph:
> **Orientation correction (2026-06-13).** Li2024's prognostic direction is **adverse** (high CMag →
> *worse* 5-yr survival, ~1.5× increased risk; `question:0077`, `paper:Li2024a`), **not** protective.
> Earlier records (incl. this plan's first draft and `interpretation:0004/0006`, `proposition:0007`)
> had it reversed. So **HR > 1 = adverse = agrees with Li2024**; **HR < 1 = protective = contradicts
> Li2024.** The locked criteria below use the corrected orientation; see
> `pre-registration:0002-t046-metabric-cmag-ueda-validation` for the binding contract.

title: Seasonal rhythms in human physiology, omics, biomarkers, cognition, and immunity
paragraph: A central, underappreciated finding across this corpus is that modern electric lighting has almost entirely suppressed the seasonal photoperiodic signal in industrialised populations. Stothard2017 demonstrated this directly: under modern electric lighting, melatonin onset, midpoint, offset, and duration were statistically indistinguishable between winter and summer (all p ≥ 0.15). Under natural light at the same latitude (~40°N), biological night expanded by more than 4 hours in winter versus summer — a seasonal amplitude that parallels the melatonin duration expansion seen in well-studied seasonal mammals. One week of winter backcountry camping advanced melatonin onset by 2.6 hours; a single weekend camping advanced it by 1.4 hours (~69% of the full week effect). The implication for seasonal biology is profound: biomarker studies in industrialised cohorts face a paradox in which the seasonal zeitgeber inputs are attenuated relative to the evolutionary baseline, yet the downstream seasonal outputs (immune composition, endocrine phasing, cognitive neural costs) remain detectable, suggesting either high sensitivity of the remaining photoperiod signal, thermal/metabolic seasonal input

title: CGMacros within-person clock-time glucose confound (free-living proxy)
paragraph:
**Classification-relevance overlay:** translate the fasting amplitude into a clinically interpretable
statement — would the within-person fasting clock-time swing move a person across an ADA fasting-glucose
cutpoint (IFG ≥100, diabetes ≥126 mg/dL)? This is the H02-relevant "shift a classification" framing.

title: For which antihypertensive pharmacokinetic profiles does time-of-day dosing
paragraph: TIME (Mackenzie 2022) enrolled patients on their usual antihypertensive medications — a heterogeneous mix dominated by agents with elimination half-lives of 12–50 hours (amlodipine ~35–50 h, lisinopril ~12 h, losartan/irbesartan ~11–15 h). For such agents, shifting dosing by 12 hours produces a small and relatively flat change in trough-to-peak drug concentration across the 24-h cycle. The PROBE design recorded only a ~1.8 mmHg morning SBP difference. This raises a pharmacokinetic question: does a PK half-life threshold exist below which dosing time reliably produces a meaningful 24-h BP profile difference and, by extension, a plausible therapeutic benefit from chronological alignment with the nocturnal risk window?

title: GynCycle period sensitivity — the menstrual period is a distributed emergent property of the HPO loop, not a single rate-limiting node; the FSH-synthesis 'higher FSH → shorter cycle' law is not reproduced
paragraph:
But the cross-model check also **falsifies the universality of the node-weighting**. The
DDE node ranking (Σ|S| share) is **follicular 49% > fsh 17% > luteal 15% > lh_surge 12% >
estradiol 6%** — where GynCycle was lh_surge 34% > follicular 20% > GnRH 18% > estradiol
13% > luteal 7% ≫ fsh 1%. The **invariant** is that follicular development is a top-2 node
and no node is a rate-limiter in either; the **divergence** is the dominant node
(surge/E₂ in GynCycle, follicular in the DDE). Concretely, the DDE **reproduces "higher
FSH → shorter cycle"** (`VFSH` is the 2nd-ranked, widest-range lever, 24.4–36.2 d) — the
very law GynCycle did *not* reproduce. So two of this interpretation's headline GynCycle
findings (surge-weighted distribution; FSH period-inert) are **model-specific**, while the
distributed/no-rate-limiter core is **cross-model**. The transferable claim is the absence
of a single controller, not the node ranking.

title: GynCycle global (Morris+Sobol) sensitivity corroborates the distributed-emergent menstrual period — no total-effect dominator (max ST 0.32), additive period, Morris-flagged candidates refuted by Sobol
paragraph:
This **supports** `proposition:0010` by running the exact falsification test that
`evidence-line:0016` named as able to overturn it: a global / interaction (Morris +
Sobol) decomposition that could reveal a parameter or node dominating the *total-effect*
index even with a modest local OAT |S|. No such dominator was found. Over the joint
±10% hypercube of all 114 natural-cycle parameters, Morris μ\* (the all-114 screen)
ranking tracks the t055 OAT |S| ranking (Spearman 0.88); the top parameter carries only
6.5% of total μ\*; and the Sobol total-effect index — computed on the top-12 Morris
movers with the rest pinned at baseline — has max **ST = 0.32 ≪ 1** with
max(ST − S1) = 0.015 (additive period). The two Morris movers that *did* fall outside the
OAT top-15 (`k_AF3_E2`, `T_E2_freq`) have huge σ/μ\* (boundary nonlinearity) and
**negligible top-K Sobol ST ≈ 0.001** — strongly consistent with a boundary/nonlinearity
artifact rather than a confirmed controller. This establishes "no total-effect dominator
found by the all-114 Morris screen + top-12 Sobol confirm," not a full 114-parameter
Sobol exclusion under all pinned-parameter interactions — the residual is the cross-model
gap, not

title: Human Connectome Project — Young Adult (S1200) neuroimaging with season-of-acquisition
paragraph:
The HCP Young Adult 1200-Subjects release (~1113 imaged, healthy adults 22–37, scanned
2012–2015): 3T/7T structural MRI, resting + task fMRI, dMRI, MEG (subset), and behavior. For
seasonal-confounding work the relevant feature is the **acquisition-quarter field** in the
release metadata, which lets subjects be binned into season — the approach used by Wang et al.
2023 (*Sci Rep*) to derive four seasonal groups (n=410). Exact scan dates live in the
Restricted tier; the open tier (free ConnectomeDB account + click-through terms) supplies the
imaging plus the quarter-level season proxy.

title: Part of the cardiometabolic variance attributed to chronological aging is reproductive-stage
paragraph:
Belief here is held at `moderate`, not strong. The "X% of aging *is* stage" decomposition is a
statistical partition under collinear age/stage in an observational panel and is model-class
dependent (pooled OLS differs in level). The composite-clock follow-up (t023) closes the earlier
"clock *inputs*, not a clock" caveat and rules out the pre-committed *informative-null*
(aggregation-cancellation) reading, but does **not** raise confidence as a new source: it is the
same SWAN cohort/markers (`independence_group: swan`, `shared-source`), and the KDM clock is weak
(`r_char`≈0.13), so the propagation is partly mechanical. The dominant residual uncertainty is now
**cross-cohort replication** — all support collapses into one cohort. Only the age functional-form
objection (t022) and the aggregation-cancellation objection (t023) are closed.

title: Pre-registration — METABRIC independent validation of the clean-room Ueda CMag index (t046 q77 part 1)
paragraph:
No Bonferroni/FDR across the family: the headline rests on 2 pre-specified correlated co-primaries
adjudicated by the direction grid, and the sensitivities are robustness re-fits of the *same*
hypothesis, governed by the pre-committed arbitration rule rather than treated as independent screens.
The verdict-bearing α is 0.05 two-sided on the per-SD primaries, with CIs (not p-thresholds) carrying
the power-aware labels.

title: GynCycle period sensitivity — the menstrual period is a distributed emergent property of the HPO loop, not a single rate-limiting node; the FSH-synthesis 'higher FSH → shorter cycle' law is not reproduced
paragraph:
The "local OAT only" limitation below has since been **closed** by a global Morris +
Sobol sensitivity run ([[gyncycle-global-sensitivity-distributed]], `evidence-line:0017`,
`results/gyncycle-global-sensitivity/`). Over the joint ±10% hypercube of all 114
parameters, the all-114 Morris μ\* screen tracks the OAT |S| ranking (Spearman 0.88) and
no parameter carries > 6.5% of total μ\*; the Sobol total-effect index (computed on the
top-12 Morris movers, the rest pinned at baseline) has max **ST = 0.32 ≪ 1** with the
period response essentially additive (max ST − S1 = 0.015). The two Morris movers that
fell outside the OAT top-15 (`k_AF3_E2`, `T_E2_freq`) have negligible top-K Sobol
ST ≈ 0.001 — consistent with boundary/nonlinearity artifacts, not confirmed hidden
dominators. So no total-effect dominator was found by the all-114 Morris screen + top-12
Sobol confirm (short of a full 114-parameter Sobol exclusion); the distributed-emergent
verdict **survives** the global + interaction test. New nuance: no *single* ±10%
perturbation breaks the cycle (0/114) but **9.7%** of the *joint* ±10% box does —
interactions govern cycle *existence* near the boundary, not period *control*. The

title: Natural-postmenopause shifts lipids and insulin resistance net of chronological
paragraph: In the SWAN longitudinal panel (3,200+ women, ~14k modeled person-visits), natural postmenopause vs premenopause shifts cardiometabolic biomarkers holding chronological age fixed. Adjusted random-intercept model (M2b, +BMI+race): total cholesterol +7.9 mg/dL (p=1e-15), LDL +4.7 (p=7e-8), triglycerides +9.3% (p=5e-12), HOMA-IR +7.5% (p=4e-5). The within-person fixed-effects model (M3), which differences out every time-invariant between-woman confounder, tracks these in raw units: tchol +7.4 (p=6e-9), LDL +4.5 (p=1e-4), trig +8.7% (p=2e-8), HOMA-IR +6.3% (p=4e-3). The shift therefore survives the strongest available confounding control and is not stable between-woman confounding.

title: GynCycle menstrual period shows no rate-limiting parameter under ±10% OAT sensitivity; sensitivity is loop-distributed, surge-weighted
paragraph:
Fine sweeps (0.5×–1.5×) of the four task-named candidate levers:
`k_Ih_FSH` (V_FSH) flat (28.0–28.2 d, S = +0.002, rank 92 — the "higher FSH → shorter
cycle" law is **not** reproduced and the weak sign is reversed); `T_E2_LH` (Km,LH surge
threshold) 26.9–28.5 d (S = +0.047, rank 46, longer-when-higher); `k_AF2_AF3`
(follicular mass-transfer) 27.4–29.1 d (S = −0.063, rank 35, shorter-when-higher);
`k_cl_Lut4` (corpus-luteum decay) **26.1–35.1 d** (S = −0.222, rank 23,
shorter-when-higher) — the widest-range lever among the fine-swept candidates (the 4
named nodes + top-5 local movers; not a claim over all 114 params), i.e. the luteal
timer is tunable in the model. All perturbations across all four sweeps stayed stable
(21/21 each).

paragraph: **Verdict:** [⌀] Non-adjudicating — the fasting clock-time cosinor *did* discriminate (Dexcom amplitude 8.93 mg/dL, 95% CI [6.84, 11.53], well-powered at MDE 3.5, negative control clean), but the **`device_dependent` veto fires** (Libre 3.43 mg/dL, acrophase shifted 4.77 h on the *same* N=45), deliberately closing the rollup per `pre-registration:0005`. **No belief update to `hypothesis:0002`.**

title: Does natural variation in the CK1 phosphoswitch set inter-individual circadian
paragraph: The CK1 phosphoswitch is the core period-setting mechanism in the mammalian circadian clock: CK1delta/epsilon anchored to the PER CK1-binding domain phosphorylates competing sites on PER that either target it for proteasomal degradation (Degron) or stabilize it via product inhibition of the kinase (FASP). Philpott et al. 2023 resolved the structural basis of pFASP-mediated CK1 feedback inhibition and showed that CRISPR disruption of the FASP priming serine shortens period by ~2–3 h in human cells. Known Mendelian variants at both nodes (FASP S662G and tau R178C in CK1delta) produce extreme sleep-phase phenotypes. The question is whether the continuous distribution of common variants affecting FASP phosphorylation efficiency, CK1 anchoring strength, or phosphatase opposition contributes to the full inter-individual range of circadian period (~23.5–24.5 h in healthy humans) and whether that period variation translates into measurable health differences (chronotype-associated disease risk, metabolic rhythm quality, treatment response windows).
